title: Connection-pool posture per deploy target: long-lived pool on Node, request-scoped pool on container, delegated to Hyperdrive on Workers-adjacent (v1.1.0)
context: Postgres has real connection cost per open (TCP handshake, TLS negotiation, authentication, role setup). A long-lived Node process wants one pool per process amortising that cost across every request. A request-scoped container platform (a serverless-container target spinning fresh instances per request) cannot hold a long-lived pool because the instance dies at request end; each instance opens a pool for its request budget. A Workers-adjacent target via the round-6 Hyperdrive v1.1.0 adapter delegates the pool entirely to Cloudflare's Hyperdrive-managed pool.
decision: The pool posture is elicited per deploy target: longLivedNode (default: long-lived pg.Pool for the process lifetime), requestScopedContainer (a pool sized to the request budget, disposed at request end), or hyperdriveManaged (reserved for the round-6 v1.1.0 adapter). The shipped defaults per posture: longLivedNode pool size 10 with idleTimeoutMillis 30000 and connectionTimeoutMillis 5000 (matching pg's own defaults); requestScopedContainer pool size 2 with idleTimeoutMillis 5000 and connectionTimeoutMillis 3000; hyperdriveManaged inherits Hyperdrive's own pool settings and holds no Node-side pool. Every default is overridable by the operator via elicited pool-config fields at apply time.
consequences: The project gets the pool posture appropriate to its deploy target without a code change: a longLivedNode app on Kubernetes and a longLivedNode app on a self-managed VM share the same shipped default; a requestScopedContainer app on a serverless-container platform gets a small per-request pool; a round-6 Workers app inherits Hyperdrive's pool. The pool-posture-smoke probe drives twenty concurrent queries at pool size 5 and asserts no timeout; the probe does not impose a sizing formula so operator overrides are safe. Standards trace clause: generic enterprise practice.

alternativesConsidered.name: One pool posture (longLivedNode) for every target
alternativesConsidered.summary: Ship the long-lived pool as the only posture; a request-scoped container platform holds the pool for the instance lifetime.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: A fresh-per-request container that holds a long-lived pool re-pays the connection cost on every instance. Sizing the pool for a request-scoped instance is different from sizing it for a long-lived process; conflating them under one default surprises the operator.

alternativesConsidered.name: Delegate every pool to Hyperdrive from v1.0.0
alternativesConsidered.summary: Ship Hyperdrive as the pool manager for every target.
alternativesConsidered.reasonNotChosen: Hyperdrive is a Cloudflare-account-bound service; forcing every project to bind to Cloudflare before applying the blueprint conflicts with the local-first posture (round-5 spec ruling 5, maintainer decision). Round 6 lands Hyperdrive as an elicit for the operator who wants it.
